expectations.text: The feedback stops at the first structural failure; it does NOT deliver a full audit covering all four Parts of the checklist

Did not dump all four parts."

expectations.text: The feedback contains no item-by-item scoring table and does not output or fill in the self-check card
expectations.evidence: no verbatim evidence found; judged from overall reading — the feedback.md is prose only (总体判断 / 做得好的地方 / 第一个结构性失败 / 一处具体改法), with no scoring table or self-check card present.

expectations.text: The feedback identifies the final sentence of the closing (the one containing 「感谢有你的关注」 / 「比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」) as conclusion + named-emotion, i.e. an explanation-mode leak (4.2 / S.1)
expectations.evidence: "又往下写了一句总结："但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨……这种感觉比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心。"这句话在替读者下结论、告诉读者该有什么感受（"更持久""更开心"）"

expectations.text: The proposed fix is minimal (deletion or reordering, not wholesale rewriting). The landing line may be EITHER the pivot 「但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨」 OR the perception line 「声音太响太多，我分不清」 — both are acceptable. HARD condition: the pivot line's content must survive somewhere in the revised text. Moving it earlier passes; deleting it entirely fails
expectations.evidence: The fix deletes the pivot line entirely rather than preserving it: "把"但我能确定的是……"那整句收掉，直接接"今天就到这里吧，我们下周再见"。" The revised text lands on the perception line and jumps straight to the sign-off, so the pivot content 「但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨」 does not survive anywhere. HARD condition violated: "deleting it entirely fails."

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT accuse the pivot 「但我能确定的是」 of violating 4.1 — using the disturbance as a contrast/turn is not the same as explaining the disturbance itself, since the sound remains unidentified
expectations.evidence: The critique of the pivot is aimed at the concluding/named-emotion tail, not at 4.1 explaining the disturbance: "这句话在替读者下结论、告诉读者该有什么感受（"更持久""更开心"）". No claim that the disturbance/sound was explained away; on the contrary it praises "一个精确的、没有被解释掉的感知事实".

expectations.text: The feedback recognizes the piece is a newsletter rather than a fiction scene, and does NOT ask the author to add a suspense-style disturbance or rewrite the close to hook-standard
expectations.evidence: "落在了一句对读者说的暖心结论上" and "这个技法" framing; the fix only removes a sentence and keeps the sign-off "今天就到这里吧，我们下周再见", asking for no added suspense/disturbance. no verbatim evidence found for an explicit 'newsletter not fiction' statement; judged from overall reading that it treats the piece as newsletter prose and imposes no hook-standard rewrite.

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT raise R as a finding or warning about the author's rhythm across issues. Merely citing an R principle to grant an exemption (e.g. 'a quiet close is fine; not every issue needs a hook') is acceptable and does NOT violate this expectation
expectations.evidence: no verbatim evidence found; judged from overall reading — the feedback contains no mention of rhythm-across-issues (R) as a finding or warning.

expectations.text: The feedback includes at least one specific, reasoned positive observation (e.g. 「声音太响太多，我分不清」 is a perceived fact, not a feeling word) rather than generic praise
expectations.evidence: "雨停之后窗外传来"像蛙鸣的声音"，你自己都分不清是蛙是虫（"只是声音太响太多，我分不清"）。这正是这个技法要的东西：一个精确的、没有被解释掉的感知事实。"

expectations.text: If the feedback offers a rewritten ending, it does NOT introduce a double-uncertainty, sympathy-fishing formulation such as 'I don't even know how many people are reading this'
expectations.evidence: The proposed ending lands on "声音太响太多，我分不清" then "今天就到这里吧，我们下周再见"; no sympathy-fishing / 'don't know how many are reading' formulation appears.

claims.claim: The buried perception line reads "只是声音太响太多，我分不清"
claims.evidence: Quoted consistently in both the working-well section and the fix; used as the proposed landing line.

claims.claim: Deleting the pivot sentence and connecting directly to the sign-off is the minimal fix
claims.evidence: It is minimal in edit-size but violates the eval's HARD condition that the pivot line's content survive; a reordering (moving the pivot earlier) would have satisfied both minimality and survival.

suggestions.assertion: The proposed fix is minimal ... HARD condition: the pivot line's content must survive somewhere in the revised text.
suggestions.reason: This is the discriminating assertion and it correctly caught the failure mode: the run produced a plausible-looking minimal fix (cut one sentence) that nonetheless deletes the pivot the reader is meant to leave on. Good, load-bearing assertion — keep it.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are strong and discriminating. The pivot-survival HARD condition is what separates a correct minimal fix from a lossy one; this run passed 8/9 but failed exactly there.
